She wears a light-purple cardigan over a pink top and a navy pleated skirt; she rests her cheek on one hand and looks sideways at her friend with a bored, unhappy face. On the right, a girl with long, wavy dark hair and gold hoop earrings sits on the edge of the bed; she wears an open blue shirt over an orange top and wide white trousers, and she talks happily, both hands open as she explains something. Folded sweaters (cream, blue, black and pink) lie on the bed beside her. Shopping bags stand around the room: pink, cream and blue bags on a small table by the window, and another pink bag on the floor at the front right.

passage.traditional: 學校附近有一家咖啡廳，以前{1}不太好，客人很少。{2}吸引學生，老闆想出了一個辦法：學生買一杯咖啡，就可以在店裡念一個下午的書，還可以免費上網。這個辦法很有用，客人{3}了很多。現在平日下午，店裡的位子都滿了，{4}週末也一樣。
passage.simplified: 学校附近有一家咖啡厅，以前{1}不太好，客人很少。{2}吸引学生，老板想出了一个办法：学生买一杯咖啡，就可以在店里念一个下午的书，还可以免费上网。这个办法很有用，客人{3}了很多。现在平日下午，店里的位子都满了，{4}周末也一样。
passage.pinyin: Xuéxiào fùjìn yǒu yì jiā kāfēitīng, yǐqián shēngyì bú tài hǎo, kèrén hěn shǎo. Wèile xīyǐn xuéshēng, lǎobǎn xiǎng chū le yí ge bànfǎ: xuéshēng mǎi yì bēi kāfēi, jiù kěyǐ zài diàn lǐ niàn yí ge xiàwǔ de shū, hái kěyǐ miǎnfèi shàngwǎng. Zhège bànfǎ hěn yǒuyòng, kèrén zēngjiā le hěn duō. Xiànzài píngrì xiàwǔ, diàn lǐ de wèizi dōu mǎn le, lián zhōumò yě yíyàng.
passage.english: There's a café near school. Business used to be poor, with few customers. To attract students, the owner came up with an idea: a student who buys one coffee can study in the café all afternoon and use the internet for free. The idea worked: customers increased a lot. Now on weekday afternoons all the seats are taken, and even at weekends it's the same.

questions.why: 生意不太好: business was poor, which is why there were few customers.
為了 + purpose, then the action: to attract students, the owner came up with an idea.
客人增加了很多: after the idea, the number of customers went up a lot.
連週末也一樣: even at weekends the seats are all taken, as on weekday afternoons.

passage.traditional: 我家附近的夜市有一位賣衣服的老闆。以前他的衣服賣得不太好，一個晚上只能賣幾件。後來他{1}，很多年輕人喜歡韓式{2}，就開始賣韓國流行的毛衣和帽子。現在他的客人{3}了不少。他說，年輕人很容易被流行的東西{4}，做生意就要懂他們的心理。
passage.simplified: 我家附近的夜市有一位卖衣服的老板。以前他的衣服卖得不太好，一个晚上只能卖几件。后来他{1}，很多年轻人喜欢韩式{2}，就开始卖韩国流行的毛衣和帽子。现在他的客人{3}了不少。他说，年轻人很容易被流行的东西{4}，做生意就要懂他们的心理。
passage.pinyin: Wǒ jiā fùjìn de yèshì yǒu yí wèi mài yīfu de lǎobǎn. Yǐqián tā de yīfu mài de bú tài hǎo, yí ge wǎnshàng zhǐ néng mài jǐ jiàn. Hòulái tā fāxiàn, hěn duō niánqīngrén xǐhuān hánshì fúzhuāng, jiù kāishǐ mài Hánguó liúxíng de máoyī hé màozi. Xiànzài tā de kèrén zēngjiā le bù shǎo. Tā shuō, niánqīngrén hěn róngyì bèi liúxíng de dōngxi xīyǐn, zuò shēngyì jiù yào dǒng tāmen de xīnlǐ.
passage.english: At the night market near my home there's a stall owner who sells clothes. His clothes used to sell poorly; he could only sell a few a night. Then he noticed that lots of young people like Korean-style clothing, so he started selling the sweaters and hats that are in fashion in Korea. Now he has quite a few more customers. He says young people are easily attracted by what's in fashion, so to do business you have to understand how they think.

questions.why: 後來他發現: he noticed what young people like, and that gave him the idea.
韓式服裝: Korean-style clothing, which is why he started selling Korean sweaters and hats.
客人增加了不少: his customers went up quite a bit. 變成 needs what they became (變成很多人 is not said like this).
被流行的東西吸引: young people are attracted by what's in fashion (被 + doer + 吸引).

text.traditional: 我的室友以前很少看電視，可是因為她男朋友的關係，她最近愛上了日劇。她男朋友是日本人，一開始常常帶她一起看，還會告訴她日劇裡的人在說什麼。現在她不但每天都看，還開始學日文了。她說，後年想去日本遊學。
text.simplified: 我的室友以前很少看电视，可是因为她男朋友的关系，她最近爱上了日剧。她男朋友是日本人，一开始常常带她一起看，还会告诉她日剧里的人在说什么。现在她不但每天都看，还开始学日文了。她说，后年想去日本游学。
text.pinyin: Wǒ de shìyǒu yǐqián hěn shǎo kàn diànshì, kěshì yīnwèi tā nánpéngyǒu de guānxì, tā zuìjìn àishàng le Rìjù. Tā nánpéngyǒu shì Rìběn rén, yìkāishǐ chángcháng dài tā yìqǐ kàn, hái huì gàosu tā Rìjù lǐ de rén zài shuō shénme. Xiànzài tā búdàn měi tiān dōu kàn, hái kāishǐ xué Rìwén le. Tā shuō, hòunián xiǎng qù Rìběn yóuxué.
text.english: My roommate used to watch very little TV, but because of her boyfriend she has recently fallen for Japanese dramas. Her boyfriend is Japanese; at first he often had her watch with him and told her what the people in the dramas were saying. Now she not only watches every day but has also started learning Japanese. She says she'd like to go on a study tour in Japan the year after next.

Nánpéngyǒu cháng péi tā yìqǐ kàn.

questions.why: 因為她男朋友的關係: her boyfriend is the cause. He is Japanese and at first watched the dramas with her. Learning Japanese came after she started watching, the study tour is her own plan, not her boyfriend's, and she used to watch little TV.

text.traditional: 學校附近有一家冰店，老闆做的芒果冰很有名。今年因為天氣的關係，芒果很少，價錢也很貴，老闆只好每碗多收二十塊。以前一碗一百塊，現在變成一百二十塊。可是客人還是很多，每天下午不到四點，芒果冰就賣光了。
text.simplified: 学校附近有一家冰店，老板做的芒果冰很有名。今年因为天气的关系，芒果很少，价钱也很贵，老板只好每碗多收二十块。以前一碗一百块，现在变成一百二十块。可是客人还是很多，每天下午不到四点，芒果冰就卖光了。
text.pinyin: Xuéxiào fùjìn yǒu yì jiā bīng diàn, lǎobǎn zuò de mángguǒ bīng hěn yǒumíng. Jīnnián yīnwèi tiānqì de guānxì, mángguǒ hěn shǎo, jiàqián yě hěn guì, lǎobǎn zhǐhǎo měi wǎn duō shōu èrshí kuài. Yǐqián yì wǎn yìbǎi kuài, xiànzài biànchéng yìbǎi èrshí kuài. Kěshì kèrén háishì hěn duō, měi tiān xiàwǔ bú dào sì diǎn, mángguǒ bīng jiù mài guāng le.
text.english: There's an ice shop near school whose mango ice is famous. This year, because of the weather, mangoes are scarce and expensive, so the owner has had to charge 20 dollars more a bowl. A bowl used to be 100; now it's 120. But there are still lots of customers, and every afternoon the mango ice is sold out before four.

prompt.simplified: 下面哪一个是对的？

choices.traditional: 今年的芒果冰比較便宜

choices.pinyin: Mángguǒ bīng sì diǎn yǐhòu cái mài guāng.
choices.english: The mango ice only sells out after four.

questions.why: 因為天氣的關係，芒果很少: the weather is why mangoes are scarce (and dear). The text never says the weather brought more customers (客人還是很多 only says there are still many), the ice now costs 20 more, and it sells out before four (不到四點).

text.traditional: 我弟弟最近上課常常打瞌睡。老師以為他生病了，媽媽以為他每天念書念得太晚，大家都很擔心。後來我才發現，他每天晚上都在房間裡看美國影集，看完已經半夜了。現在媽媽把他的電腦放在客廳，十點以後就不讓他用了。
text.simplified: 我弟弟最近上课常常打瞌睡。老师以为他生病了，妈妈以为他每天念书念得太晚，大家都很担心。后来我才发现，他每天晚上都在房间里看美国影集，看完已经半夜了。现在妈妈把他的电脑放在客厅，十点以后就不让他用了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ dìdi zuìjìn shàngkè chángcháng dǎ kēshuì. Lǎoshī yǐwéi tā shēngbìng le, māma yǐwéi tā měi tiān niànshū niàn de tài wǎn, dàjiā dōu hěn dānxīn. Hòulái wǒ cái fāxiàn, tā měi tiān wǎnshàng dōu zài fángjiān lǐ kàn Měiguó yǐngjí, kàn wán yǐjīng bànyè le. Xiànzài māma bǎ tā de diànnǎo fàng zài kètīng, shí diǎn yǐhòu jiù bú ràng tā yòng le.
text.english: My younger brother has been nodding off in class a lot lately. His teacher thought he was ill, and Mom thought he was studying too late every night; everyone was worried. Then I found out that every night he watches American TV series in his room, and by the time he finishes it's midnight. Now Mom keeps his computer in the living room and doesn't let him use it after ten.

prompt.traditional: 弟弟上課打瞌睡，是因為什麼？
prompt.simplified: 弟弟上课打瞌睡，是因为什么？
prompt.pinyin: Dìdi shàngkè dǎ kēshuì, shì yīnwèi shénme?
prompt.english: Why does the brother nod off in class?

choices.pinyin: Tā shēngbìng le.
Tā niànshū niàn de tài wǎn.
Tā kàn yǐngjí kàn de tài wǎn.
choices.english: He watches TV series too late.

choices.pinyin: Tā zài dānxīn kǎoshì.

questions.why: 他每天晚上都在房間裡看美國影集，看完已經半夜了: he stays up late watching series. Being ill and studying late are only what the teacher and Mom wrongly thought (以為); the worrying in the text is the family's, about him.

text.traditional: 上個月我去花蓮玩，想買一些名產送給朋友做紀念。可是那天是星期一，很多名產店都沒開，我只好在火車站的便利商店買了幾盒小蛋糕，打算把它們送給朋友。回到台北以後，我才發現，台北的便利商店也有一樣的小蛋糕，價錢還便宜十塊。
text.simplified: 上个月我去花莲玩，想买一些名产送给朋友做纪念。可是那天是星期一，很多名产店都没开，我只好在火车站的便利商店买了几盒小蛋糕，打算把它们送给朋友。回到台北以后，我才发现，台北的便利商店也有一样的小蛋糕，价钱还便宜十块。
text.pinyin: Shàng ge yuè wǒ qù Huālián wán, xiǎng mǎi yìxiē míngchǎn sòng gěi péngyǒu zuò jìniàn. Kěshì nà tiān shì xīngqíyī, hěn duō míngchǎn diàn dōu méi kāi, wǒ zhǐhǎo zài huǒchē zhàn de biànlì shāngdiàn mǎi le jǐ hé xiǎo dàngāo, dǎsuàn bǎ tāmen sòng gěi péngyǒu. Huí dào Táiběi yǐhòu, wǒ cái fāxiàn, Táiběi de biànlì shāngdiàn yě yǒu yíyàng de xiǎo dàngāo, jiàqián hái piányí shí kuài.

But that day was a Monday and many specialty shops were closed, so I had to buy a few boxes of little cakes at the convenience store in the train station, planning to give them to my friends. Back in Taipei, I found that the convenience stores in Taipei have the same little cakes, and ten dollars cheaper too.

choices.pinyin: Shì Huālián cái yǒu de míngchǎn.
choices.english: They're a specialty found only in Hualien.

text.traditional: 我爸爸以前對夜市沒有興趣，他覺得那裡人太多、太擠，也不太乾淨。上個月，我帶他去吃了一次臭豆腐，他就越來越喜歡逛夜市了。現在他每個週末都要去，還常常帶媽媽一起去。他說，夜市的小吃又便宜又好吃，比餐廳的菜有意思多了。
text.simplified: 我爸爸以前对夜市没有兴趣，他觉得那里人太多、太挤，也不太干净。上个月，我带他去吃了一次臭豆腐，他就越来越喜欢逛夜市了。现在他每个周末都要去，还常常带妈妈一起去。他说，夜市的小吃又便宜又好吃，比餐厅的菜有意思多了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ bàba yǐqián duì yèshì méiyǒu xìngqù, tā juéde nàlǐ rén tài duō, tài jǐ, yě bú tài gānjìng. Shàng ge yuè, wǒ dài tā qù chī le yí cì chòu dòufǔ, tā jiù yuè lái yuè xǐhuān guàng yèshì le. Xiànzài tā měi ge zhōumò dōu yào qù, hái chángcháng dài māma yìqǐ qù. Tā shuō, yèshì de xiǎochī yòu piányí yòu hǎochī, bǐ cāntīng de cài yǒu yìsi duō le.
text.english: My dad used to have no interest in night markets; he thought they were too crowded, too packed and not very clean. Last month I took him to eat stinky tofu once, and he has come to like going to night markets more and more. Now he wants to go every weekend and often takes Mom along. He says night-market snacks are cheap and tasty, and much more interesting than restaurant food.

text.traditional: 昨天我跟朋友約好晚上七點在電影院門口見面。我六點半就到了，可是等了一個小時，她都沒來。我打電話給她，她說她記錯了，以為我們約的是今天晚上。她覺得很不好意思，說今天要請我看電影，還要請我吃晚飯。
text.simplified: 昨天我跟朋友约好晚上七点在电影院门口见面。我六点半就到了，可是等了一个小时，她都没来。我打电话给她，她说她记错了，以为我们约的是今天晚上。她觉得很不好意思，说今天要请我看电影，还要请我吃晚饭。
text.pinyin: Zuótiān wǒ gēn péngyǒu yuē hǎo wǎnshàng qī diǎn zài diànyǐngyuàn ménkǒu jiànmiàn. Wǒ liù diǎn bàn jiù dào le, kěshì děng le yí ge xiǎoshí, tā dōu méi lái. Wǒ dǎ diànhuà gěi tā, tā shuō tā jì cuò le, yǐwéi wǒmen yuē de shì jīntiān wǎnshàng. Tā juéde hěn bùhǎoyìsi, shuō jīntiān yào qǐng wǒ kàn diànyǐng, hái yào qǐng wǒ chī wǎnfàn.
text.english: Yesterday my friend and I arranged to meet at 7 p.m. at the cinema entrance. I got there at 6:30, but I waited an hour and she never came. I phoned her, and she said she'd got it wrong: she thought we had arranged to meet this evening. She felt very bad and said that today she'll treat me to a movie and to dinner too.
